relevance.rationale: Derives an explicit formula for the colored Jones polynomial J_K(n) of the 2-bridge knot S(p,t), with a more explicit form for twist knots, and deduces a relation between the degree of the colored Jones polynomial and the crossing number for two specific 2-bridge families. This matters here because the corpus's deuteron closure is 6_2, which its own bibliography note identifies as two-bridge with fraction 11/3, and the 5_2 knot used in the one-loop cross-check probe is likewise two-bridge. The corpus currently depends on the two-bridge property only through a cited literature theorem about the one-loop invariant and adjoint torsion; it has no direct colored-Jones computation for these knots at all -- a grep for 'two-bridge'/'2-bridge' across computations/ returns nothing. An explicit closed formula for J_{S(p,t)}(n) would let the corpus compute rather than cite for exactly the knots its deuteron argument rests on. Supporting rather than core: the corpus's existing claims are literature-backed and not in doubt, so this converts an assumption into a check rather than fixing an error. The degree-versus-crossing-number corollary is stated for two specific families and I have not verified that 6_2 lies in either, so no claim is made about it here.

keyResults.locator: Sec. 1 and the main formula for J_{S(p,t)}(n)
keyResults.statement: An explicit formula is given for the colored Jones polynomial of the 2-bridge knot S(p,t) in Schubert notation, specialising to a more explicit form for twist knots.
keyResults.useForFolio: Enables a direct colored-Jones computation for 5_2 and 6_2 -- the corpus's one-loop cross-check knot and its deuteron closure -- where the corpus currently has only a literature dependency and no compute.

proposedActions.rationale: The corpus leans on the two-bridge property of 6_2 for a literature-backed torsion result but registers no reference giving the colored Jones of two-bridge knots explicitly.

Evaluate the explicit two-bridge formula for 5_2 = S(7,3) and compare with the corpus's existing 5_2 cross-check probe. This verifies an existing witness with an independent formula; no external number is adopted, and a disagreement is the finding.
